findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Mark the post-merge runner-seconds report as an explicit post-merge follow-up (with owner/tracking) so the landing gate does not depend on a run that only exists after merge.
evidence: 'For the first post-merge Verify run, compute each changed cell delta...'
'inspect resolved command lines and savings on the next Verify run after merge'
findings.finding: AC 'The first post-merge Verify report applies the stated per-cell and summed runner-seconds formula' cannot be evaluated in-session — it requires a Verify run that only exists after the change merges, which the plan itself defers in step 7 ('the next Verify run after merge').
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria line 21; Plan step 2 and step 7
scenarios: Reviewer tries to check the acceptance criterion at merge time but the post-merge Verify run has not yet occurred
findings.suggested_fix: Split AC 21 into (a) in-session: the workflow change lands with the formula documented, and (b) a labeled post-merge follow-up that records the actual deltas on the ticket after the first Verify run.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reframe step 3 as an open survey and state the decision path if the expected consensus (>=2 matches, no documented rejection) does not hold.
evidence: 'OSS consensus means at least two of these three projects selectively collect coverage on a primary or dedicated configuration...'
asserted-not-derived: the survey result is stated as fact rather than as a finding to be established
findings.finding: Step 3 asserts the survey outcome as a foregone conclusion ('OSS consensus means at least two of these three projects selectively collect coverage... and none documents rejecting that practice') before the survey is actually performed, coupling a data-gathering task to a predetermined result. If the survey finds fewer than two matches or a documented rejection, ACs 12-13 and the step conflict.
scenarios: Executor performs the survey and discovers only one of the three projects matches, or finds a documented rejection
findings.suggested_fix: State step 3 as 'Survey Django/NumPy/SciPy and report findings' and specify the fallback (e.g. escalate/re-justify) if fewer than two match or a rejection is documented, rather than asserting the outcome.

findings.checklist_item: Reframe the OSS-survey acceptance criteria to report what the survey actually finds (including a contrary finding) rather than requiring a predetermined 'two of three match / none rejects' outcome.
evidence: Plan text: 'OSS consensus means at least two of these three projects selectively collect coverage... and none documents rejecting that practice'
The AC is phrased as an outcome to satisfy, not a question to answer
findings.finding: The OSS-survey step and its acceptance criteria hardcode the expected result ('at least two of three projects selectively collect coverage', 'none documents rejecting that practice'). This is a predetermined-conclusion research mechanism: it asserts the answer before the survey runs, so the step cannot be honestly completed if the actual findings diverge, and it invites confirmation-shaped reporting rather than an open investigation.
findings.location: Plan: 'Survey Django, NumPy, and SciPy...'; ACs 'At least two of the three named OSS projects match...' and 'No surveyed project documents rejecting...'
scenarios: The survey finds only one project matches, or finds a documented rejection — the AC as written becomes unsatisfiable, pressuring the author to over-read the evidence
The precedent (f3d4) landed on measured cost alone with no OSS survey, so the survey is not load-bearing to the decision yet is gated on a fixed answer
findings.suggested_fix: Change the ACs to 'the survey records each project's coverage-collection topology and any documented rationale, and the decision is reconciled against those findings' so a contrary result is a valid, reportable outcome.

findings.checklist_item: Reframe the OSS survey as an open verification: report per-project findings (workflow file + link) as-found and state the decision rule and fallback if fewer than two projects match or any documents a reliability-driven rejection, rather than asserting the 'at least two of three' outcome up front.
evidence: Plan text: 'OSS consensus means at least two of these three projects selectively collect coverage on a primary or dedicated configuration while broader compatibility cells run uninstrumented, and none documents rejecting that practice for coverage or reliability.'

Retrieved source (Django contributor docs, docs.djangoproject.com internals/contributing/writing-code/unit-tests): 'The CI coverage job runs tests using PostgreSQL on Ubuntu' — corroborates selective single-cell coverage for Django, but does not establish the NumPy/SciPy outcome.
ABSENCE: the plan provides no fallback for the case where the survey finds fewer than two matches or finds a documented rejection — the AC is written as if the result is already known.
findings.finding: The plan asserts the prior-art survey's conclusion as a predetermined pass/fail gate ('OSS consensus means at least two of these three projects selectively collect coverage... and none documents rejecting that practice') rather than framing the Django/NumPy/SciPy survey as an open verification whose findings are reported as-found. Django's practice is independently confirmable (its contributor docs describe a single dedicated Ubuntu/PostgreSQL CI coverage job), but the NumPy and SciPy outcomes are asserted, not established; if real evidence diverges (only one match, or a documented rejection) the plan's own acceptance criteria force a contradiction.
findings.location: Plan step 3 ('Survey Django, NumPy, and SciPy current CI workflows...') and Acceptance Criteria lines 'At least two of the three named OSS projects match selective coverage collection' / 'No surveyed project documents rejecting selective coverage collection'
scenarios: The survey finds only Django clearly matches and NumPy/SciPy use aggregated matrix coverage instead, leaving the 'at least two of three' criterion unmet after the work is done.
A surveyed project's tracker records a past reliability-driven reversal of selective coverage, which the plan's AC declares must not exist.

evidence: 1 criterion line(s) bundle multiple deliverables with 'and' (split so each is independently verifiable).
findings.suggested_fix: Split compound criteria, replace subjective terms with observable outcomes, and state how each is verified.

findings.checklist_item: State a positive rationale for making Ubuntu Python 3.13 (rather than the requires-python floor 3.11 or 3.12) the single coverage-collecting cell, or justify collecting on the floor interpreter instead.
evidence: Plan repeatedly fixes on 'Ubuntu Python 3.13 alone collects branch coverage and enforces fail-under' with no stated reason for 3.13 specifically
Precedent f3d4 kept coverage on all three ubuntu cells; the matrix comment (line 294-297) notes 3.11 is the requires-python floor (enum.StrEnum)
search_files confirmed src/rebar has no sys.version_info branches, so no cell has a distinct coverage verdict — making the selection arbitrary unless justified
findings.finding: The plan designates Ubuntu Python 3.13 as the sole coverage-collecting cell but states no positive rationale for choosing 3.13 over the requires-python floor (3.11) or 3.12. Because that one cell becomes the only place fail-under is enforced, the choice is load-bearing; a defensible alternative — collecting on the oldest supported interpreter (3.11), where coverage-relevant interpreter/stdlib divergence is likeliest to surface — is neither chosen nor ruled out.
findings.location: Plan: 'Encode the condition...' / 'Update the coverage rationale...'; AC 'Ubuntu Python 3.13 collects branch coverage'
scenarios: A future coverage-relevant divergence appears only on 3.11 (the floor) and goes untraced because coverage moved to 3.13
Reviewers cannot tell whether 3.13 was a deliberate or incidental pick
findings.suggested_fix: Add one sentence in the rationale-comment/docs update explaining the cell choice (e.g. 'the newest interpreter is chosen because X'), or switch the coverage cell to Ubuntu 3.11 as the conservative floor and say why.
